California is entering the most perilous stretch of its year-round fire season, when hot, arid winds roll down from the mountains and out to sea. item.title: Apple-OpenAI Judge Says He’s ‘Likely’ to Side With iPhone Maker
item.description: The judge in Apple Inc.’s high-stakes trade-secret theft case against OpenAI said he’s “highly likely” to grant the iPhone maker an injunction barring use of its proprietary information by former employees now at the artificial intelligence startup. The judge in San Jose, California, is also hearing a separate demand by OpenAI to dismiss Apple’s lawsuit entirely. Apple sued OpenAI, its hardware chief and a former iPhone hardware engineer in July, accusing them of conspiring to extract confidential information from former Apple employees related to product design, manufacturing, component technologies, testing methodologies and the company’s supply chain.

item.title: NY City Accuses Law Firm of Running Injury Claims Fraud Operation
item.description: New York City is suing a Manhattan law firm for allegedly running a multimillion dollar personal injury fraud scheme by filing as many as 15 injury claims against the city on behalf of people allegedly harmed due to roadway defects. The city accuses the law firm Asher & Associates, P.C. The city maintains that when it or other defendants have confronted Asher & Associates with the contradictory evidence, the law firm has discontinued the cases without explanation.

item.title: FSB finalises sound practices for the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)
item.description: Press enquiries: +41 61 280 8477 [email protected] Ref: 14/2026 The Financial Stability Board (FSB) today published its final report on Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence , reflecting public feedback received on a consultative version of the report, published in June 2026. As AI technologies and applications evolve, the FSB will monitor developments and update the sound practices as necessary to support safe and responsible AI adoption by financial institutions. The FSB launched a public consultation on its proposed sound practices for the responsible adoption of A I in June 2026.

item.title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Overview of consultation responses
item.description: On 10 June 2026, the FSB published a consultation report on Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The objective of the consultation was to gather stakeholder feedback on the proposed sound practices to help financial institutions adopt AI responsibly. The FSB received around 160 responses to the consultation, which ended on 22 July 2026.

item.title: Insurance-linked securities expand the horizon for impact investing: Smith, Sage Advisory
item.description: Speaking yesterday at the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference, Bob Smith, President & Co-CIO of fixed income and alternative solutions manager Sage Advisory, explained that he sees insurance-linked securities as an asset class that can expand the horizon of impact investing. “So, through the mechanism and the risk transfer mechanism offered by ILS, I think you expand the horizon for impact investing, and I think that is where the focus needs to be, because there’s a lot of money out there looking for this product, looking for this area of the market to invest in.” You can read more of the firm’s thoughts on the impact topic in this article: ILS & cat bonds show impact investing can move beyond mitigation into resilience: Sage Advisory . Smith is a strong proponent for investing into catastrophe bonds and other natural catastrophe linked insurance-linked securities, seeing them as particularly valuable diversifiers that over the long-term have also outperformed many other fixed income asset classes.

item.title: KCC estimates hurricane Isaias wind and surge insured losses at $3bn
item.description: Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), estimated that insured losses from wind and storm surge from hurricane Isaias will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range. Catastrophe risk modelling specialist Karen Clark & Company (KCC) has provided an initial estimate for the private insurance market loss from wind and storm surge associated with recent hurricane Isaias, saying it expects the total to be $3 billion. This latest estimate for the recent hurricane impacts on the Gulf Coast can be compared to one from Verisk, which recently gave its initial industry insured loss estimate for Isaias, saying that onshore property losses from the storm could reach $2 billion .

item.title: Markel strengthens Marine & Energy Liability team in London
item.description: The pair will be based in London and report to the Marine & Energy Liability team, part of the Marine Transportation business, led by Grant Smith. Markel Insurance, the insurance operation within Markel Group Inc., has appointed Josephine Stroud as Head of Energy Liability and Jenny McFarlane as Senior Underwriter for Marine & Energy Liability. The two key appointments aim to strengthen Markel’s London Market underwriting team and follow the establishment of Markel’s new Marine Transportation business within its London Market operations.

item.title: SCOR finds European captive insurers hold median solvency ratio of 221%
item.description: SCOR, a global reinsurance company providing risk management solutions, has published its latest analysis of Europe’s captive insurance and reinsurance market, examining financial strength, premium trends and solvency positions using year-end 2025 Solvency II data. The median solvency ratio was 221%, indicating that eligible own funds were more than twice the regulatory Solvency Capital Requirement. SCOR’s benchmarks are intended to help captive owners and insurance professionals compare their financial and solvency positions with those of similar organisations.

item.title: People Moves: Marsh Hires Meta’s Risk Manager for New Role
item.description: Crowley joins Marsh from Meta, where he spent 10 years as a risk manager, leading the company’s insurance and risk management programs, including an owner-controlled insurance program for its data centers, which covered over $200 billion in construction values. Marsh said Michael Crowley has joined the firm as senior enterprise risk advisor for digital infrastructure. In this newly created role, Crowley will help digital infrastructure clients manage risk and build resilience throughout the full lifecycle of their projects, from development and contracting through construction and operations.

item.title: Eight States Sue OpenAI, Claiming ChatGPT Harms Children
item.description: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others. Attorneys general from the states, which include Iowa, Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn the trust of users. The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works.

item.title: Viewpoint: AI Doesn’t End the Rite of Passage; the Grind Wasn’t the Teacher
item.description: Then, almost overnight, the conversation flipped and the new worry is how AI will wipe out the entry-level that has long been considered a rite of passage in insurance: the processing, rekeying and repetitive work that junior people grind through before they get to the more interesting parts of the job. It was a rite of passage, and I don’t regret it. The assumption is that taking away that grind also takes away how people learn the business.

item.title: Constellation Re completes first Bermuda transaction
item.description: Constellation Re Bermuda has completed its inaugural reinsurance transaction, an intercompany deal covering term life, universal life, and disability income products. The Bermuda-domiciled licensed reinsurer also received an “A” insurer financial strength rating from Fitch Ratings, which designated it a core entity within the Constellation group. The platform expands Constellation Re’s ability to offer reinsurance across different geographies and regulatory jurisdictions, helping insurers manage risk and capital.

item.title: Zurich launches sports event ticket insurance with Hakuna
item.description: Zurich Group Germany has entered the standalone ticket insurance market through a partnership with embedded insurance startup Hakuna and Hanover-based event organizer eichels. The partners plan to assess expanding the ticket insurance model to other organizers and event formats following the initial launch. Zurich carries the risk, while Hakuna handles policy issuance, contract management, and claims settlement.

item.title: Artemis Group to acquire ERGO Pro
item.description: ERGO Beratung und Vertrieb has agreed to sell ERGO Pro to Artemis Group. Artemis will hold a majority stake, while ERGO Pro’s current management and leading sales partners will become additional shareholders. The company will also distribute ERGO products in other lines alongside products offered by Artemis’ MGAs.

item.title: OneShield Appoints Terry Brown Chief Insurance Officer
item.description: Marlborough, MA — October 14, 2026 – OneShield , whose core systems and AI platform help property and casualty insurers and MGAs modernize how insurance work gets done, has appointed Terry Brown as Chief Insurance Officer. Agents can do the work, but someone has to know what good insurance work looks like, and nobody knows that better than Terry.” The appointment comes as OneShield continues to build AI-native capabilities for underwriting, claims, and billing operations across its P&C insurer and MGA customer base. In this newly created role, Brown will work side by side with OneShield’s leadership team and its customers to shape the company’s AI-native capabilities and bring them to market.

item.title: San Diego PD Considers Using AI to Write Police Reports
item.description: Earlier this year, the San Diego Police Department made headlines for a policy that prohibited officers from using artificial intelligence to produce police reports. A request for information issued by the department on July 31 describes the department looking for a program “that utilizes AI technology to assist officers and investigators in writing police reports.” “The goal of this initiative is to enhance efficiency in report writing, thereby allowing officers to respond more quickly to calls for service,” the request for information reads. In December, the department forbade officers from using AI platforms to generate reports.

Using those records, along with competitors’ promotions and social media trends, Marklo suggests what a brand should market next. item.title: Cat bonds offer flexibility across fixed income and alternative investment allocations: Victory Capital
item.description: Given that catastrophe bonds are known for having a low correlation to traditional financial markets, global asset management firm Victory Capital has highlighted how the asset class’s portfolio implementation flexibility makes it viable for either an investor’s fixed income allocation or its alternative investment strategy. Thus, we think that the true risk profile of cat bonds is one of the misunderstood aspects of this fixed income asset class,” Victory Capital explained. In a recent article, Victory Capital outlines that many investors prioritise the incorporation of strategies with returns that either have low or no correlation to other major asset classes, along with securing new sources of income that have the potential to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns regardless of what’s happening across the broader financial market.

item.title: PICC P&C announces first sidecar issuance in Hong Kong
item.description: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited (PICC P&C) has issued the first insurance-linked securities (ILS) in the form of a sidecar in Hong Kong, providing quota-share reinsurance protection for offshore windfarm insurance risks in mainland China. The deal follows PICC P&C’s issuance of a catastrophe bond in Hong Kong in 2022, marking another step in the insurer’s use of international capital markets to diversify insurance risks. PICC P&C acted as sponsor, issuing sidecar notes through Great Wall Re Limited, a Hong Kong special purpose insurer.

item.title: Constellation Re Bermuda completes first reinsurance transaction, receives ‘A’ Fitch rating
item.description: Constellation Re, a provider of M&A and reinsurance solutions and member of the Constellation family of businesses, has revealed the completion of the first reinsurance transaction for Constellation Re Bermuda, Ltd., its Bermuda-domiciled licensed reinsurer, which has also been assigned an insurer financial strength rating of ‘A’ by Fitch Ratings. Alongside the transaction, Fitch Ratings has assigned an insurer financial strength rating of ‘A’ to the Bermuda reinsurer, noting its role as a core entity within the wider Constellation group. Scott Shepherd, president and CEO of Constellation Re, commented: “The completion of CRBL’s inaugural transaction and the assignment of an ‘A’ rating from Fitch mark important milestones in the continued growth of our reinsurance business.

item.title: Marsh and Bloomberg New Economy establish coalition to address global risks
item.description: Marsh, a global professional services firm, and Bloomberg New Economy, a platform focused on global economic and business issues, have launched a new coalition aimed at helping organisations respond to emerging risks and identify opportunities for sustainable economic growth. The organisations that gain clarity first do more than survive disruption — they move faster, invest with confidence, and gain ground while others are still assessing.” Marsh and Bloomberg New Economy said the coalition would use executive discussions, research and thought leadership to examine the risks facing businesses and economies. Marsh and Bloomberg New Economy have identified five priority areas for the coalition’s initial programme.

item.title: Trump’s AI Liability Push Opens Blame Game for Models Gone Rogue
item.description: The Trump administration’s embrace of legal liability to enforce artificial intelligence safety sets the stage for future conflicts over who foots the bill when AI models go rogue: the companies that design the systems or the people that deploy the technology. The administration’s liability push fits into Trump’s largely hands-off approach toward regulating AI, a technology whose growth is central to his economic agenda. President Donald Trump, in spurning new AI safeguards, has taken it a step further, saying the Justice Department should intervene if models get out of hand.

item.title: Novacore to acquire Diesel Insurance Solutions to add cross-border trucking cover
item.description: The post Novacore to acquire Diesel Insurance Solutions to add cross-border trucking cover appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Novacore has agreed to acquire Diesel Insurance Solutions, a California-based managing general underwriter specialising in cross-border trucking, physical damage, and cargo insurance. The acquisition will add a dedicated cross-border trucking and cargo platform to Novacore’s Specialty Transportation segment.

item.title: EY announces alliance with INSTANDA to help insurers modernise core architecture for the AI era
item.description: It’s about supporting organizations to become more agile, more resilient and better equipped to capitalize on whatever comes next, with the freedom and agency to evolve at the pace customers and markets demand.” The post EY announces alliance with INSTANDA to help insurers modernise core architecture for the AI era appeared first on Insurtech Insights . The EY organization has announced an alliance between INSTANDA, one of the leading AI-augmented no-code insurance platforms, and Ernst & Young LLP (EY UK) to help insurers execute transformation at scale, unlock the potential of AI, and support their people to provide greater value across the business. Together, the organisations aim to help insurers reduce architectural complexity, modernise core operations, and create the foundations required for long-term agility and sustained technology adoption.

Progressive’s PIF count fell by about 3k policies from August to September. Year-to-date, Progressive’s net income stands at $8.6 billion and combined ratio sits at 87.5%.

item.title: Liberty Mutual to acquire Austral Seguradora
item.description: Liberty Mutual announced an agreement to acquire Austral Seguradora, a top-five Brazilian surety provider headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. Under the agreement, Liberty Mutual will retain Austral’s portfolio without business or broker disruption, and its approximately 100 employees will join Liberty when the deal closes. Bringing together Austral’s market expertise with Liberty’s global strength positions us to grow, deepen our relationships with brokers and clients, and deliver even greater value across Brazil and the wider region.” – Manuel Moreno, Liberty Mutual president and chief underwriting officer, LatAm & US, Liberty Specialty Markets.

item.title: Gold Body Accused of Enabling Deaths at Tanzanian Gold Mine
item.description: The London Bullion Market Association’s certification program served as a “thick smokescreen” that enabled serious abuses at a Tanzanian gold mine where two men died, lawyers alleged at the start of a London trial that could threaten its existence. Lawyers for the two families argue that the gold body’s decisions had a direct effect on the use of violence at the mine. Holding the body accountable for the deaths could pose an existential threat to the association and its Responsible Gold Guidance scheme, which aims to ensure that supply chains are free of human rights abuses and conflict, they added.
